title: Water/Wastewater Engineers
description: Design or oversee projects involving provision of potable water, disposal of wastewater and sewage, or prevention of flood-related damage. Prepare environmental documentation for water resources, regulatory program compliance, data management and analysis, and field work. Perform hydraulic modeling and pipeline design.

clusters.label: Drafting, Laying Out, and Specifying Technical Devices, Parts, and Equipment

tasks.text: Design domestic or industrial water or wastewater treatment plants, including advanced facilities with sequencing batch reactors (SBR), membranes, lift stations, headworks, surge overflow basins, ultraviolet disinfection systems, aerobic digesters, sludge lagoons, or control buildings.
Design pumping systems, pumping stations, pipelines, force mains, or sewers for the collection of wastewater.
Design water distribution systems for potable or non-potable water.
Identify design alternatives for the development of new water resources.
Design water runoff collection networks, water supply channels, or water supply system networks.
Design water or wastewater lift stations, including water wells.
Perform hydrological analyses, using three-dimensional simulation software, to model the movement of water or forecast the dispersion of chemical pollutants in the water supply.
Design water storage tanks or other water storage facilities.
Design sludge treatment plants.
Perform mathematical modeling of underground or surface water resources, such as floodplains, ocean coastlines, streams, rivers, or wetlands.
Review and critique proposals, plans, or designs related to water or wastewater treatment systems.
Conduct cost-benefit analyses for the construction of water supply systems, runoff collection networks, water and wastewater treatment plants, or wastewater collection systems.
Analyze storm water or floodplain drainage systems to control erosion, stabilize river banks, repair channel streams, or design bridges.

Perform hydraulic analyses of water supply systems or water distribution networks to model flow characteristics, test for pressure losses, or to identify opportunities to mitigate risks and improve operational efficiency.
Analyze the efficiency of water delivery structures, such as dams, tainter gates, canals, pipes, penstocks, or cofferdams.
Conduct water quality studies to identify and characterize water pollutant sources.
Conduct feasibility studies for the construction of facilities, such as water supply systems, runoff collection networks, water and wastewater treatment plants, or wastewater collection systems.
Gather and analyze water use data to forecast water demand.
Conduct environmental impact studies related to water and wastewater collection, treatment, or distribution.

clusters.label: Providing Consultation and Advice to Others

tasks.text: Analyze and recommend chemical, biological, or other wastewater treatment methods to prepare water for industrial or domestic use.
Provide technical support on water resource or treatment issues to government agencies.
Analyze and recommend sludge treatment or disposal methods.
Provide technical direction or supervision to junior engineers, engineering or computer-aided design (CAD) technicians, or other technical personnel.
Oversee the construction of decentralized or on-site wastewater treatment systems, including reclaimed water facilities.
Evaluate the operation and maintenance of water or wastewater systems to identify ways to improve their efficiency.
Design or select equipment for use in wastewater processing to ensure compliance with government standards.
Develop plans for new water resources or water efficiency programs.
Write technical reports or publications related to water resources development or water use efficiency.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Science
skills.def: Using scientific rules and methods to solve problems.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Operations Analysis
skills.def: Analyzing needs and product requirements to create a design.

skills.name: Management of Personnel Resources
skills.def: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Computer aided design CAD software
skills.def: Software to design 2D or 3D objects. May include engineering or architectural features. Examples: Autodesk AutoCAD, Autodesk AutoCAD Civil 3D, Autodesk Revit, Bentley GEOPAK Civil Engineering Suite.

skills.name: Analytical or scientific software
skills.def: Software to capture data, perform analysis, or generate reports or visualizations to support scientific research. Examples: Bentley StormCAD, DHI MIKE URBAN, EPA Storm Water Management Model SWMM, HEC-1.

skills.name: Geographic information system
skills.def: Software to capture, manage, analyze, or display geographically-referenced information. Examples: ESRI ArcGIS software, ESRI software, Geographic information system GIS software, Geographic information system GIS systems.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Business software applications, Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint.
